h: Cushing disease (pituitary adenoma): high-dose dexamethasone result and ACTH?
p: Pituitary adenomas retain partial feedback, so high-dose dexamethasone suppresses cortisol (ACTH normal or high). Adrenal tumors have low ACTH; ectopic ACTH (small cell lung cancer) does not suppress.

h: How does carbonic anhydrase speed up its reaction?
d: Changes the delta G of the reaction
p: Enzymes lower activation energy and increase rate without altering delta G or the equilibrium.

h: Nissl staining visualizes soma and dendrites but not the axon: which organelle?
p: Nissl bodies are rough ER with ribosomes for protein synthesis; they are absent from the axon and axon hillock, and dissolve in chromatolysis after axon injury.

h: Third-trimester painful bleeding with hypertonic uterus and fetal distress: diagnosis?
p: Abruption causes painful bleeding (may be concealed), uterine tenderness and DIC risk; risks are hypertension, smoking, cocaine and trauma. Previa is painless and requires no digital exam.

h: Stays with abusive spouse, needs others to decide for her, fears being alone: diagnosis?
p: Cluster C: submissive, clingy behavior with an excessive need to be taken care of, difficulty making decisions and fear of separation.

h: Short-acting drug used to test for myasthenia gravis?
p: Edrophonium transiently improves ptosis and weakness in myasthenia (Tensilon test); pyridostigmine is the long-acting maintenance drug.

h: Sildenafil: downstream effect?
p: PDE5 inhibitors raise cGMP and smooth muscle relaxation (erection, pulmonary vasodilation). Contraindicated with nitrates (profound hypotension).

h: Cytokine recruiting neutrophils to an abscess?
p: IL-8 (CXCL8) is the main neutrophil chemoattractant; IL-5 recruits and activates eosinophils.

h: Muddy brown granular casts in a dehydrated elderly patient: renal lesion?
p: ATN (ischemic or toxic) shows muddy brown casts, FENa over 2 percent and urine osmolality near 300; prerenal azotemia has concentrated urine with low sodium.

h: Candida resistance to nystatin: mechanism?
p: Polyenes (nystatin, amphotericin B) bind ergosterol to form pores; resistance arises from decreased ergosterol. Terbinafine targets squalene epoxidase; echinocandins target beta-glucan synthase.

h: Down syndrome features with 46 chromosomes: mechanism?
p: About 4 percent of Down syndrome results from Robertsonian translocation (usually 14;21), giving 46 chromosomes; this form can be inherited from a carrier parent. The double bubble signals duodenal atresia.

h: Which test shows the spatial distribution of CD117 (c-KIT) in tissue?
p: IHC stains protein in tissue sections, preserving architecture; GISTs are CD117 (KIT) positive and respond to imatinib.

h: Garlic breath and QT prolongation after termite poison: antidote?
p: Arsenic poisoning causes GI symptoms, garlic odor and QT prolongation; chelate with dimercaprol (BAL) or DMSA. Deferoxamine is for iron; NAC for acetaminophen.

h: Facial plethora, obesity, daytime sleepiness: cause of the redness?
a: Increased erythropoietin (from hypoxia, e.g., sleep apnea)
p: Obstructive sleep apnea causes nocturnal hypoxia, raising EPO and hematocrit; plethora results. Bradykinin increases with ACE inhibitors (cough, angioedema).

h: Resistance to activated protein C: mutation?
p: Factor V Leiden (R506Q) is the most common inherited thrombophilia; factor Va resists cleavage by activated protein C, raising DVT/PE risk.

h: Status epilepticus first-line drug (benzodiazepine): mechanism?
a: Increases frequency of GABA-A chloride channel opening
p: Benzodiazepines increase opening frequency; barbiturates increase duration. IV lorazepam is first-line, then phenytoin or levetiracetam.

h: Competitive inhibitor: effect on Km and Vmax?
p: Competitive inhibitors raise apparent Km and can be overcome by more substrate, so Vmax is unchanged; noncompetitive inhibitors lower Vmax.

h: BPH: which drug shrinks the prostate?
p: 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors reduce DHT-driven growth over months. Alpha-1 blockers relax smooth muscle for faster symptom relief without changing size.

h: Fewer voltage-gated K+ channels: effect on the myocardial action potential?
p: Potassium efflux drives repolarization (phases 3); blocking it prolongs the action potential and QT interval (class III antiarrhythmics).

h: Hemorrhagic shock: renal response?
p: Low perfusion activates the sympathetic system and RAAS, raising proximal sodium and water reabsorption and conserving volume; GFR falls.

h: Streptococcus gallolyticus (bovis) endocarditis: associated condition to look for?
p: S. gallolyticus (group D, bile-esculin positive, not enterococcus) endocarditis warrants colonoscopy. Viridans streptococci follow dental procedures.

h: Pop, locking and pain with external rotation after a tackle: injured structure?
p: Meniscal tears cause joint-line tenderness, locking and positive McMurray; the medial meniscus is injured with the ACL and MCL in the unhappy triad.

h: Tall teen with severe acne, aggression, learning difficulty: karyotype?
p: XYY: tall stature, severe acne, learning and behavior problems, usually normal fertility; often unrecognized (nondisjunction in paternal meiosis II).
